sections.h2: Which Saginaw County office does what on a tax bill?
sections.html:
Three layers handle a Saginaw County tax bill. A city or township assessor sets the value, a city or township treasurer sends the bill, and the County Treasurer takes over once taxes turn delinquent. Michigan leaves assessing with local governments, so the name and phone number on your assessment notice or tax bill beat any county number for questions about value or a due date.

The County Treasurer's office is in Room 107 of the courthouse, 111 S. Michigan, Saginaw, MI 48602. The phone is (989) 790-5225, and the office is open weekdays from 8:00 am to 5:00 pm. Besides delinquent real property tax, the Treasurer runs the Delinquent Tax Revolving Fund, administers the county hotel and motel tax, and chairs the Land Bank Authority that manages tax foreclosed properties. Ask your city or township treasurer for the summer and winter due dates, because the county page does not publish them.

  • Value, exemptions and the March appeal: the assessor in your city or township.
  • Current summer and winter bills: the local treasurer shown on the bill.
  • Delinquent balances and tax certificates: Saginaw County Treasurer, (989) 790-5225.
  • Recording a deed: Saginaw County Register of Deeds, (989) 790-5270.

sections.h2: How are Saginaw County properties valued, and how do owners appeal?
sections.html:
State law assesses property at 50% of true cash value. Taxable value, which the tax rate is applied to, rises each year by the lesser of 5% or inflation until a sale resets it (MCL 211.27a). Your notice shows both numbers, and an owner can appeal the assessed value but not the cap itself.

The March Board of Review meets on the second Monday of March, and every board must hold at least 12 hours that week, including evening hours, to hear protests (MCL 211.30). The board then sends each protester a written decision by the first Monday in June along with the right to go on to the Michigan Tax Tribunal. A township or city can also allow protests by letter, and a nonresident owner can file by letter regardless.

The City of Saginaw notes that July and December boards sit only when there are errors or poverty exemptions to decide. Each local unit sets its own schedule, so check with your assessor before assuming a date.

sections.h2: What happens when Saginaw County taxes go delinquent?
sections.html:
Delinquent real property tax moves to the County Treasurer, who collects it in person, by mail or online. The office accepts cash, money order and certified check at the counter, and personal checks are accepted only for first-year delinquencies up to January 1. Visa, MasterCard and Discover are accepted, and a mailed payment goes to Saginaw County Treasurer, 111 S. Michigan Avenue, Saginaw, MI 48602.

Online payment works around the clock through an outside vendor, with an access fee on the total. The county's card policy has a few rules worth knowing:

  • A government photo ID must accompany a card payment, and the card must belong to the named payer.
  • If a payment is reversed or declined, it is treated as void and all fees, interest and forfeiture fees reapply from the original date.
  • A voided payment that had a redemption certificate recorded adds $20 for the correction.
  • Overpayments under $3 are rounded into interest, and any refund goes back to the card used.
  • Payments post to the parcel you name, with no refund for paying the wrong parcel.

Saginaw County also took part in a class action settlement over surplus proceeds from tax foreclosure auctions held between 2013 and 2020. The claim deadline, July 16, 2026, has passed.

sections.h2: How does a sale change a Saginaw County tax bill?
sections.html:
A sale resets taxable value to the state equalized value for the next year, and the buyer must notify the local assessor within 45 days on the state form. Because Saginaw County's median owner-occupied home is older and less costly than many in Michigan, the reset can be smaller in dollars than in the Detroit suburbs, but it applies the same way. Transfers to a spouse, to a parent, child or grandchild for residential use, and certain trust and estate transfers are not counted as a transfer of ownership.

At recording, a warranty deed also needs a treasurer's certificate. The County Treasurer's list prices it at $5 for up to five descriptions and $1 for each additional description, and state law requires proof that taxes for the five preceding years are paid (MCL 211.135). A quitclaim deed with no warranty is excepted. Anyone selling a house with delinquent taxes should get a payoff figure from the Treasurer before setting a closing date.

sections.h2: What is the county like for owners and buyers?
sections.html:
Saginaw County covers 816 square miles in Mid-Michigan, drained by rivers that join into the Saginaw River. The 2020 census counted 190,124 residents and 78,442 households. Of the 85,953 housing units, 8.7% were vacant, and 70.5% of occupied homes were owner-occupied. Residents were 41.3 years old at the median, and one household in three was a single person.

The cities are Saginaw, Frankenmuth and Zilwaukee, and the rest of the county is villages and townships, including Birch Run, Chesaning, Kochville and Swan Creek. Interstates 75 and 675 serve the metro area, with US 23 and M-13, M-46 and M-47 filling in the grid. MBS International Airport sits near Freeland.

A parcel's school district changes the bill. Saginaw Public Schools and Saginaw Township Community Schools cover the largest urban areas, while Frankenmuth, Chesaning Union, Birch Run Area, Freeland Community, Hemlock Public, Swan Valley and Bridgeport-Spaulding each serve their own territory. Saginaw Valley State University and Delta College anchor higher education.

sections.h2: What should a Saginaw County seller line up before closing?
sections.html:
Start with the local treasurer for any open current-year bill, then call the County Treasurer about delinquent years. Ask for a written payoff, since interest and forfeiture fees can change the total. Then tell the title company whether the deed will carry a warranty covenant, so the certificate is ordered. After closing, the buyer files the transfer form with the assessor, and the register of deeds at (989) 790-5270 records the deed.

Sellers with a house that needs repairs or a tenant still in place can ask the assessor about the value effect, but the tax bill is owed regardless of condition. The Treasurer's office can explain its partial-payment practice and hardship options for those who are behind.

faqs.q: Who sends the property tax bill in Saginaw County?
faqs.a: Your city or township treasurer sends it. The County Treasurer takes over delinquent real property tax, at (989) 790-5225.

faqs.q: When does the March Board of Review meet in Saginaw County?
faqs.a: State law has it meet on the second Monday of March, with more sessions that week. Your local assessor's office posts the exact schedule.

faqs.q: Can I pay Saginaw County delinquent taxes online?
faqs.a: Yes. The County Treasurer takes online payments 24 hours a day through an outside vendor, with an access fee. Cards require the named payer's government ID at the counter.

faqs.q: What does a sale do to the next tax bill in Saginaw County?
faqs.a: Taxable value resets to the state equalized value for the following year. The buyer notifies the local assessor within 45 days.

faqs.q: How do I get a tax certificate for a Saginaw County deed?
faqs.a: Ask the County Treasurer in Room 107 of the courthouse. The fee is $5 for up to five descriptions and $1 for each additional one.
